items.title: A morphism of affine formal algebraic spaces is of finite type exactly when the ring map is taut and topologically of finite type
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: For a continuous map of weakly admissible topological rings over a scheme, the lemma states that the induced morphism of affine formal algebraic spaces is of finite type if and only if the ring map is taut and the target ring is topologically of finite type over the source (statement lines 6342-6350). The proof fixes a common framework: tautness corresponds to representability, and both spaces are written as filtered colimits of the spectra of their quotients by weak ideals of definition, the target's quotients being the closures of the images of the source's (proof lines 6352-6358). For the direction from the ring-theoretic condition, one chooses a ring map from a polynomial algebra with dense image, notes that it remains dense after passing to any of the quotients and hence is surjective there, and then for a quasi-compact test scheme over the source -- which factors through one of the quotients -- identifies the base change of the morphism with the base change of the corresponding map of affine schemes, which is of finite type (proof lines 6360-6374). For the converse one picks a quotient of the source, uses the hypothesis to see that the corresponding maps of quotients are of finite type, lifts images of generators back to the target ring, and shows the resulting polynomial map has dense image by comparing two quotients and applying the criterion for surjectivity modulo a locally nilpotent ideal (proof lines 6376-6391). The claim is H2: two implications are proved, each resting on a different observation -- the first on the compatibility of the presentations and the second on the comparison of two quotients through a surjectivity criterion.
